DESCRIPTION: Names the application or software being used. Common examples are web servers and application servers like Apache, Tomcat, and WebLogic.

DESCRIPTION: Describes the role of the service or component within the architecture. Examples include web servers, application servers, caching systems, and APIs.

DESCRIPTION: Indicates the criticality or priority level of the service. Tier 0 typically represents the most critical services, while higher numbers indicate lower criticality.
BUSINESS VALUE: Essential for prioritizing monitoring efforts, resource allocation, and incident management based on the criticality of the service.

DESCRIPTION: Classifies the backup and recovery strategy for the service. Bronze, Silver, and Gold often represent increasing levels of backup frequency and retention.
BUSINESS VALUE: Important for ensuring data protection and business continuity, helping to manage risk and meet recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO).

DESCRIPTION: Specifies the underlying platform or ecosystem on which the service operates. Examples include middleware solutions, broader technology ecosystems, or shared platforms.
BUSINESS VALUE: Critical for understanding the infrastructure dependencies, facilitating integration, and ensuring compatibility and standardization across services.

DESCRIPTION: Identifies the business product or application domain. Examples include customer relationship management (CRM) systems and content management systems (CMS).

DESCRIPTION: Describes the network segment where the service is running. DMZ (demilitarized zone), internal, and external networks are common examples.

DESCRIPTION: Identifies the type of data handled by the service. Examples include financial data, PHI (protected health information), and PII (personally identifiable information).
